title: Prefill-aware architecture fingerprint heuristic for kernel family warmstart
creator: Nadia Park
description: Goal: Build a lightweight, prefill-first heuristic that picks a compact candidate set of kernel families at RPC arrival time using a short architecture fingerprint + sequence-length distribution snapshot, then warmstarts microbenchmarks only for the top candidates. Motivation: Full online probing for every request is too costly for mixed workloads; current large-scale kernel selection probes increase p50 and p99 tails for small bursts. This ticket implements an intermediate approach that trades a tiny amount of extra memory (cached fingerprints + microprobe cache) for faster, more stable kernel choices and reduced warmup noise. The heuristic must be conservative (no SLO regressions), compatible with warmstart cache eviction, and able to be A/B rolled with canary percentage gating.
tasks: Define architecture fingerprint vector (SM version, memory bandwidth bucket, L2 size, on-chip matrix dims) and seq-len histogram features (prefill deciles + short-run burst indicator)
Implement feature extractor in runtime hot-path (<= 20µs overhead target) and telemetry event schema
Design kernel family scoring function: weighted linear score + penalize quantized fallback when seq-len > threshold
Microprobe runner that accepts candidate list and runs short decode-only latency checks with a tight timeout and records median/99th
Warmstart cache integration: cache key = fingerprint_hash + model_variant + seq_bucket; eviction LRU TTL; size budget 2k entries per node
Experiment harness and dashboards: per-route AB test, p50/p95/p99 latency, token/sec, and token-cost delta vs baseline
Rollout plan: feature flag -> 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback if p99 increases beyond 5% or cost > 3%
acceptance_criteria: Runtime extractor adds <20 microseconds to RPC path at 99th percentile
Can warmstart top-2 candidates within 50ms in 95% of cases for prefill-heavy routes
Net p50 latency improvement >= 4% on mixed prefills in internal benchmark (same or better p99)
No more than 2% increase in token CPU/GPU cost at steady state for balanced workloads
Canary rollout automation triggers rollback when p99 regresses >5% or customer_impact flagged

2025-02-12 Rohit Malhotra: Spike results attached. Basic fingerprint (SM+mem_bw) reduced candidate set from avg 6->2 without losing best-kernel in 92% of samples. Microprobe overhead measured ~38ms when run cold; need warmstart caching to hit 50ms target. Spike notebook: https://go.redwood/confluence/runtime/spikes/prefill-fingerprint

2025-02-18 Rohit Malhotra: Design review with runtime and infra. Key trade-offs: increase fingerprint bits vs collision risk; we selected 64-bit fingerprint hash with separate human-readable telemetry. Decided on candidate-set size 3 and hedging window of 150ms for decode fallbacks.

2025-02-21 Design feedback (Anita Singh): Add explicit safety margin for Hopper-class GPUs where large tiling kernels are preferred for long seqs. Anita: 'prefer stable kernel families on Hoppers when seq > 1024 unless cost delta > 10%'.

2025-02-24 Rohit: Proto implemented. Integrated event schema in telemetry (events prefingerprint, candidate_list, microprobe_latency, selected_kernel). Hooked into per-route AB tag. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4823

2025-02-26 QA (Marcus Lee): Ran internal perf sweep on ampere/hopper/generic. Findings: For short prefills (<64 tokens) smaller kernels still win on Ampere; for seq>512 Hopper large-kernel baseline had 6-8% lower token-cost. Need policy to prefer cost over latency for background batch routes.

2025-03-02 Rohit: Updated scoring function to expose tunable weights via /config/kernel_picker. Added warmstart cache TTL metric and eviction gauge. Updated PR with unit tests. Bench dashboard (internal): https://grafana.redwood/runtime/kernel-picker/ENG-317777

2025-03-03 Nadia: Planning rollout. Canary 1% tomorrow with close monitoring on two customer-sim routes. Watch p99 latency and token-cost; if either breaches thresholds, automatic rollback enabled. Noted potential follow-up: integrate quantization-awareness into fingerprint vector.
